### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceApiAccess (10 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 49 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **66** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec4a200aa41771524f3a7c7095df404d3f6f009d` — the merge of head `853277e1dfa7f78ad3c249d32bede7e0a9f30240` into base `a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec4a200aa41771524f3a7c7095df404d3f6f009d && git checkout ec4a200aa41771524f3a7c7095df404d3f6f009d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1 853277e1dfa7f78ad3c249d32bede7e0a9f30240 && git checkout -B drift-repro a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1 && git merge --no-ff 853277e1dfa7f78ad3c249d32bede7e0a9f30240

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a75ddba178a9196c87e60025409160a40322fac1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `abe793d01950fbaeeb3ea3a96177d660c1fbed1f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/security/api-key-management-credential.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key-management-credential.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-api-key-management-credential.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-exec-ctx-principal-kind.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data-api-key-management-credential.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/request-execution-context.conformance.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/api-key-data-door-session-required.dogfood.test.ts + packages/core/src/index.ts (`export * from './security/index.js'`), packages/core/package.json (`exports`), packages/core/src/security/request-execution-context.ts (`RequestAdmission`, the `onAdmission` call), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`computeExecCtx`, `resolveExecCtx`, `apiAccessDenialFromEnable`, `mapDataError`), packages/rest/src/index.ts, packages/rest/src/{sharing,approvals,external-datasource}-routes.ts and import-template.ts (the other `/data` mounts), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (the identity step's `onAdmission`, `HttpProtocolContext.admission`), packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts and domains/mcp.ts (`buildMcpBridge`), packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts on this head and on `main`, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts (`resolveStdioExecutionContext`) and packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts (`GATED_ACTIONS`, `create`, `update`, `remove`), packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts (`apiMethods`), packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/core/CHANGELOG.md (the declaration precedents), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the declaration prompt), review of record 6495005521 on #27477 (item 15).

Face: narrowing, declared. The diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path; the floor on this face is every path of the diff outside the prose faces, and the changeset is read for ② alone. No card (disclosure ruling); the lane seat's ACCEPT covers the prose.

Security-hardening ruling: this record names positions and refusals; it carries no reproduction.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept set and the public surface the diff changes, read off the code on this head:

1. **The rule.** `apiKeyManagementCredentialRefusal({ object, operation, credential })` answers a located `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`code`, `status`, `statusCode`, `object`) only when `credential === 'api_key'`, `object === SystemObjectName.API_KEY` and the operation is outside the closed read set (`get`, `list`, `query`, `find`, `aggregate`, `history`, `export`); `undefined` otherwise. Positive on the credential, so a context told nothing keeps today's answer; every unknown verb is a write. Correct, and the one definition both doors import.
2. **REST, single-object routes.** `enforceApiAccess` asks the rule after `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` and before returning `false`, so the exposure verdict (`405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED`) comes first. Every caller of the gate hands the route's own context in: `crud-routes` (`list`, `get`, `create`, `list`, `update`, `delete`), `data-action-routes` (`clone` as `create`, `field-access` as `get`, the four `import` doors, `export`), the four per-object bulk routes (`bulk` with its child), and `rest-server.ts`'s own import gate. The parameter is required, so the type checker holds every call site; the grep over `packages/rest/src` finds no caller without it. `mapDataError` renders the refusal on the data envelope. Correct.
3. **REST, cross-object `POST /batch`.** After the per-op exposure loop (`bulk ∧ child`) and before the transaction opens, each op is asked the rule with `operation: 'bulk'`; `handleRouteError` renders it. Pinned: a batch naming `sys_api_key` is refused with the transaction never opened, and one that does not is served. Correct.
4. **The credential on REST.** `computeExecCtx` passes `onAdmission` to `resolveRequestExecutionContext`, which fires it only when `authz.userId && authz.credential` (`'api_key' | 'session'`, the `RequestAdmission` type), and stamps the value as `__admittedBy` beside `__kernel`, `__authEnvironmentId` and `__environmentId`, under the same `as any` cast, outside `ExecutionContext`. `resolveExecCtx` is memoized per request and is the one producer every data route reads (`sharing`, `approvals`, `analytics` and `batch` routes read the same method; no composition overrides it outside tests). An anonymous or key-refused request fires no admission and the rule stays silent, which is right: those are not API-key-admitted callers. Correct.
5. **The internal key and the two moved pins.** `__admittedBy` has exactly the status of `__authEnvironmentId`: an authorization input at one named reader (`enforceApiAccess`), not an `ExecutionContext` field, nothing downstream branches on it. The golden key set in `rest-exec-ctx-principal-kind.test.ts` gains it as the fourth post-assembly key and asserts `'session'` on that fixture; `request-execution-context.conformance.test.ts` sets it aside by name in `driveRest` and asserts `'api_key'` when the request led with `x-api-key` and `'session'` otherwise, and its `REST_ROW` keeps `onAdmission: undefined` because the callback shapes no field of the context. Both moves are the right ones; the conformance test's purpose (one composition, by name) is preserved. Correct.
6. **The runtime dispatcher.** `refuseUnexposedDataAction` returns at once for `executionContext?.isSystem`, judges exposure (`checkApiExposure`, the disabled-package refusal on the `'refuse'` arm), and then asks the rule off `requestContext.admission.credential`, which the dispatcher's identity step writes through the same `onAdmission` (`http-dispatcher.ts`). Reached by `handleDataRequest` (`create`, `get`, `query`, `update`) and by `callData` (`query`, `get`, `aggregate`, `create`, `update`, `delete` from `buildMcpBridge`, bound to the request's own context; the action doors and the endpoint executor too). Every read verb a caller of this gate passes is in the rule's read set; every write verb is outside it. Pinned: `/data` PATCH and `callData` refused with the protocol never asked and the dispatcher's own `errorFromThrown` rendering `403`; session, no-admission and system contexts served; reads and other objects served. Correct.
7. **Exposure first, everywhere.** `sys_api_key` declares `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'update']`, so `create`, `delete`, `bulk` and `import` answer `405` on every door before the rule is asked; the dogfood file pins `POST` and `DELETE` at `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, the REST unit test pins a narrower declaration at `405` ahead of the rule, and the dispatcher test's fixture reaches the rule through the fall-open declaration. The one write that is exposed, `update`, is the one the rule refuses. Correct.
8. **System-context writes.** The mint (`domains/keys.ts`, `ql.insert` as the system), the key-admission `last_used_at` stamp (`api-key.ts`, `ql.update` as the system) and the forced reset's revoke never pass a door's gate as a caller; the dogfood control pins both the mint and the stamp landing after the change. Correct.
9. **The `name` case.** The ADR-0092 D2 column whitelist (`revoked` alone) already refuses a member's `name` patch with the same code, so that dogfood case holds the row but is not evidence for this rule; the body says so and the ablation left it green. Judged honestly.
10. **Other `/data` mounts.** `sharing-routes` (`/:id/shares`), `approvals-routes`, `external-datasource-routes` (`/datasources/:name/external`), `import-template` (`export?template=true`) and `query-allowlist` write no row of the addressed object; none is a door to `sys_api_key`. Correct, no gap there.
11. **The stdio MCP door is not covered.** `packages/mcp`'s stdio transport resolves `OS_MCP_STDIO_API_KEY` through `resolveAuthzContext({ headers: { 'x-api-key': apiKey } })` into an `ExecutionContext` by `assembleExecutionContext` (`plugin.ts`, `resolveStdioExecutionContext`): every caller of that door is admitted by an API key, by construction. Its bridge (`stdio-data-bridge.ts`) does not run through `callData`; by its own header it mirrors `callData`'s exposure gate (`enforceApiExposure`, `GATED_ACTIONS`) and writes through the engine directly (`engine.insert` in `create`, `engine.update(object, data, { where: { id }, context })` in `update`, the same in `remove`). The `ExecutionContext` envelope carries no credential (`execution-context.zod.ts` names none), so nothing on that door can ask the rule, and nothing does: an `update_record` on `sys_api_key` (an exposed verb, item 7) from the stdio tool is served to an API-key-admitted principal exactly as before. The changeset's TO ("a write to `sys_api_key` from a request an API key authenticated is refused … on every data door"), the module docblock ("on every data door") and the body's "every user-facing door" are therefore not true of the tree. Must-fix 2.
12. **`POST /api/v1/keys` on this tree.** The branch's merge base is `4278c3b5`, 37 commits behind `origin/main`, and `79bf748ee` (#27536, the mint's interactive-session rule) is not an ancestor of it: `domains/keys.ts` on this head carries no `admission.credential !== 'session'` refusal, while `main`'s does. The docblock, the changeset and the body state the mint rule as the premise of this one; on the tree as reviewed the premise lives on `main` only. The queue merges `main` in, and nothing in this diff touches `keys.ts`, so no conflict; the sentences are true of the landed tree and not of this head. Should-fix 1.
13. **Public surface.** `@objectstack/core`'s entry does `export * from './security/index.js'`, and `security/index.ts` now re-exports `apiKeyManagementCredentialRefusal`, `API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_READ_OPERATIONS`, `API_KEY_MANAGEMENT_SESSION_REQUIRED_MESSAGE` and the type `ApiKeyManagementCredentialInput`: four new names on the package's published entry (`exports: ".", "./logger"`). That is a widened public surface; see ②. `RestServer.enforceApiAccess` is `private`; its new required `context` parameter is read by the route hosts through `RestServer['enforceApiAccess']` (an internal pick on `CrudRouteHost`, `DataActionRouteHost`, `BatchRouteHost`), and `packages/rest/src/index.ts` exports the class, not the method. A private method's signature is not a published accept set, and the body is right that this part owes no declaration. `ExecutionContext` and `packages/spec` are unchanged; `PERMISSION_DENIED` is an existing ledger code; no route is added. Correct.
14. **Message.** The refusal names the road (sign in, the API Keys page) and nothing about the key presented. Correct.

### ② Semver level

Declared on the changeset and the body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime` at `patch`; `Skills-docs: none — REASON` with a measured reading (no `skills/**` file names `sys_api_key`; the two skill mentions of "API key" are the `secret` field type).

**The `no` is wrong; the arm is right.** The diff widens the public surface of `@objectstack/core` by four names reachable from the package entry (① item 13), and the clause asks exactly that (「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」; the gate's own prompt: "`Clause-②: yes` — it widens one"). The fleet's practice on this package is consistent: an added core export is declared `yes` — `yes (widening)` for `orderHydrationBatch` / `declaredDependencyIds`, `isCloudManaged` and the position-grant readers, and `yes (narrowing)` where a narrowing rides with new exports (the app-automation elevation mark, the Default-Organization definition, `directPermissions`), all in `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md`; the review of record on #27477 judged `no` right there only because that PR's new functions were module exports not re-exported from the entry. The ADR-0087 marker already states "one export is added to `@objectstack/core`", so the changeset contradicts its own declaration line. Fix: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the changeset and the body; `Metadata-protocol: none` stays right (no authorable key, value or type moves), the three `patch` grades stay right under ruling A, and the no-major gate reads `yes` as a widening label with no level effect. Must-fix 1.

The rest of the declaration holds: the `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner; a FROM / TO naming the narrowed request (a `sys_api_key` write from an API-key-authenticated request on the generic data door), who is affected, what does not change (session, reads, system-context writes, the `405`), where the rule is decided and the embedder case; exactly one ADR-0087 HTML-comment marker in `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; and the `Skills-docs:` line. The TO's "every data door" and the module docblock's same phrase are corrected by must-fix 2, whichever way it is resolved. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- (a) **Dev's open question: reads of `sys_api_key` by an API-key-authenticated request stay open (option A).** No reason against from this review: a key reads only its owner's rows under the existing row scope, the stored hash is omitted on every read surface (#7728), and listing the owner's keys is what the API Keys list itself does; the writes are what manage a credential, and they are the two rules' subject (this one and the restore guard). A later decision can tighten reads without touching this rule's shape, since the read set is a closed list in one place.
- (b) **"The dispatcher's twin is pinned at the unit layer; the composed showcase serves `/api/v1/data` through `RestServer`."** Accepted: the dogfood file exercises the door the composition mounts, and the dispatcher's refusal is pinned through its own exits.
- (c) **The `name` case is not evidence for the rule** (① item 9). Accepted as stated.
- (d) **The mint-rule premise (#27536) is on `main`, not on this head** (① item 12). Should-fix 1: merge `origin/main` so the tree the sentences describe is the tree reviewed and the battery runs on the combined tree; the body's Verification then names that head.
- (e) **Checks on `abe793d0` at review time:** `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Spec property liveness` and the labelling runs concluded `success` (24 distinct); `Build Core`, the eight `Test Core` shards, the `Type Check` lanes, `Type Check UI` and `Build & E2E UI` were `in_progress`; nothing had failed. The landing pre-check (全绿) is the seat's read at landing, not this record's.
- (f) `open_questions`: (a) alone. Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, against the published spec on `main`: the change takes no declared capability away at the consumer and makes an existing posture real. `sys_api_key` is `managedBy: 'better-auth'`, mints only through `POST /api/v1/keys`, and exposes `update` on the data door solely so the owner's own list can revoke and restore (ADR-0092 D4, the D2 column whitelist); with #27536 the mint is a signed-in act, and a credential-lifecycle act reachable with the credential itself is the gap this closes. The shape is right: one rule in `@objectstack/core`, positive on the credential, asked at the per-object gate every route of each door already passes, after the exposure verdict so `405` keeps its place, rendered on the ADR-0112 envelope the doors already map, with the credential carried as an internal door key rather than a widened `ExecutionContext` (the right call: the envelope is a published hook surface, and this is a fact about how the context was obtained). The REST and dispatcher halves cannot drift because both import the one function and both pass their own verb vocabulary into the one read set.

What does not hold is the coverage claim. The rule is placed "where every data door passes", and the two doors named are two of three: the stdio MCP transport is a data door whose only credential is an API key and whose bridge gates exposure beside, not through, `callData` (① item 11). Either the rule is asked there too — beside `enforceApiExposure` in `create`, `update` and `remove` with `credential: 'api_key'`, which that door knows by construction, plus a pin in `packages/mcp` — or the seat rules that transport out (an operator-configured local process rather than "a request") and the changeset, the module docblock and the body stop saying "every data door" and name it as unchanged. The first is the design this PR states; the second is a different, narrower contract. Both are must-fix 2; the record does not choose. Judged per `hits` file:

- `api-key-management-credential.ts`: the rule as read; the docblock's "every data door" is corrected by must-fix 2; holds otherwise.
- `security/index.ts`: four public names; the declaration is must-fix 1; holds otherwise.
- `rest-server.ts`: gate placement, required parameter, `onAdmission` capture, the internal key's docblock; holds.
- `batch-routes.ts`, `crud-routes.ts`, `data-action-routes.ts`: every call site passes the context; the batch asks per op after exposure and before the transaction; holds.
- `action-execution.ts`: the gate after exposure, the system-context return first, the credential off `HttpProtocolContext.admission`; holds.
- The five test files: each refusal pins status, `code` and that the protocol or transaction was never asked, and each served case pins the arguments the protocol received; the dogfood file pins the row afterwards and the key's own admission before and after; the two moved pins keep their purpose; hold. Ablation evidence in the body (the rule's credential test made always-true: core 6 red, runtime 2 red, dogfood 3 red, controls green; restored and proven absent) is consistent with the pins read here; not re-run.

**Must-fix**

1. Declaration: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on the changeset and the PR body (② names the precedent spelling); keep `Metadata-protocol: none`, the three `patch` grades, the banner, the single ADR-0087 marker and the `Skills-docs:` line. Re-run `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` locally.
2. The stdio MCP door (① item 11, ④): ask `apiKeyManagementCredentialRefusal` in `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` beside `enforceApiExposure` on `create`, `update` and `remove`, with `credential: 'api_key'`, rendered as that door renders its other refusals, and pin it in `packages/mcp` (refused with the engine never asked; a read served); add `@objectstack/mcp` to the changeset. Or, on a seat ruling that the stdio transport is outside this rule, strike "every data door" from the changeset's TO, the module docblock and the body, and name the stdio transport as unchanged in the TO's "What does not change".

**Should-fix**

1. Merge `origin/main` (37 commits, `79bf748ee` among them) so the head's `domains/keys.ts` carries the mint rule the docblock, the changeset and the body cite as this rule's premise, and re-read the battery and the Verification head on the merged tree.

Implemented-by: `claude/harden-api-key-data-door`
Reviewed-by: `session_017xRBcVy4VXmkQjn2MGeaWk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

The refusal is correctly placed and complete on the two doors the PR names, the `405`-before-`403` order holds at all three gates, the internal key and the moved pins are right, the private `enforceApiAccess` signature owes no declaration, and option A on reads is sound; the FAIL is the `no` on a diff that adds four public exports (must-fix 1) and the uncovered stdio MCP door against a contract that says "every data door" (must-fix 2). A head that carries those two and nothing else owes a delta review by this reviewer, not a full round.
